meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday
facts.summary: Illinois: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Every employer shall pay the final compensation of separated employees in full, at the time of separation, if possible, but in no case later than the next regularly scheduled payday for such employee.
facts.source_title: 820 ILCS 115/5, Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act
facts.notes: Earned vacation must be paid out as part of final compensation (same section).

facts.value: at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday
facts.summary: Illinois: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Every employer shall pay the final compensation of separated employees in full, at the time of separation, if possible, but in no case later than the next regularly scheduled payday for such employee.
facts.source_title: 820 ILCS 115/5, Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Illinois basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Applicable to employers of 4 or more employees, excluding family members Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Illinois independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): Yes
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Illinois new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Illinois: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Semi-monthly; Monthly (note 2).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 2: Illinois, Nevada, New Mexico, and Virginia. Monthly payday requirements for Executive, Administrative, and Professional personnel. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Illinois is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Illinois base new employer UI rate: 2.80%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. IDES publishes a 2026 entry rate of 3.350% that includes the 0.550% fund building rate, and 3.450% for NAICS sector 56, which includes staffing (https://ides.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/ides/ides_forms_and_publications/EA-50_2026.pdf); see IL.ui.total_new_employer_rate and IL.ui.total_new_employer_rate_naics56.

facts.summary: Illinois 2026 UI contribution rate range: 0.750% to 7.050% (includes the fund building rate).
facts.evidence_quote: *All rates below include the Fund Builder ... YEAR 2016 ... 2026 ... MINIMUM RATES ... 0.750% MAXIMUM RATES ... 7.050%
facts.notes: Values read from the 2026 column of the IDES historical rate chart (the last column). Rate basis: includes fund building rate.

facts.summary: Illinois state unemployment taxable wage base: $14,250 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance

facts.summary: Illinois 2026 total new employer UI rate: 3.350% (includes 0.550% fund building rate).
facts.evidence_quote: Most employers who became liable for the payment of contributions on or after January 1, 2024 will pay at the entry rate of 3.350%.
facts.notes: Higher entry rates apply in some NAICS sectors; see IL.ui.total_new_employer_rate_naics56.

facts.applies_to: Calendar year 2026; NAICS sector 56 (includes staffing, NAICS 5613)
facts.summary: Illinois 2026 total new employer UI rate for NAICS sector 56 (Administrative Support and Waste Management, which includes staffing firms): 3.450%.
facts.evidence_quote: Administrative Support & Waste Management NAICS (sector 56) .........3.450% The above entry rate includes the 0.550% Fund Building Rate in effect for 2026.
facts.notes: Use this row for staffing and temp agencies (NAICS 5613).
